publicComments.name: Juana Martinez Gonzalez
publicComments.summary: Praised the district's COVID-19 support efforts, shared challenges as a working parent with distance learning and language barriers, and requested a meeting with board members as a parent leader with Innovate Public Schools.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton

publicComments.summary: Expressed disappointment that the community's input on the naming of Adelante Selby school was ignored in the final decision.

items.title: Approval of Construction Agreement with CalState for Roosevelt School
Discussion of School Attendance Boundary Change for Neighborhood Schools

publicComments.name: Christina Lee
publicComments.summary: Kentfield Commons resident with a 4-year-old advocated for being assigned to Henry Ford school, which is walkable, rather than Garfield, which requires crossing major roads.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Kentfield Commons resident expressed support for public education and requested assignment to the closer, more walkable Henry Ford school rather than Garfield.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Asked about current Orion enrollment numbers and questioned whether projections for 2026 were realistic given potential COVID baby boom.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to ensure boundary changes are equitable and expressed concern about packing students into already under-resourced Garfield, preferring scenario two's approach.

publicComments.name: Lisa Gianangeli
publicComments.summary: Sought clarification on whether students in the John Gill area assigned to Clifford could remain through 8th grade, and raised concerns about accurate capacity numbers accounting for special ed and child care rooms.

publicComments.name: Jacqueline Rodriguez
publicComments.summary: Hoover parent and Innovate Public Schools parent leader (translated) thanked the district, described challenges with English-only materials and ELD access, and requested a meeting with board members.

publicComments.name: Jenny Overby
publicComments.summary: Clifford parent requested that current school-of-choice families be considered in enrollment projections and asked for a review of realistic classroom capacity accounting for special uses.

publicComments.name: Ann Heinichek
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to include socioeconomic diversity as a criterion in boundary decisions, not just capacity and minimal change.

publicComments.name: Devin Mullane
publicComments.summary: Praised diversity efforts at Adelante Selby, questioned why the Peet's Harbor area was assigned to Clifford, and asked why Hoover's high capacity usage was being maintained while other schools run at 50%.

publicComments.name: Bill Brown
publicComments.summary: Argued that without a comprehensive classroom-by-classroom capacity inventory, the boundary exercise cannot be done reliably, and offered to help compile such an inventory.

publicComments.name: Vanessa De la Pascua
publicComments.summary: Spoke on behalf of the Atherwood neighborhood (including Kentfield Commons), explaining they only have access via Woodside Road and requested the board consider walkability when assigning their area to a school.

publicComments.name: Thomas
publicComments.summary: Roosevelt parent praised Roosevelt leadership, questioned why busing was provided to Roosevelt while other lower-enrollment schools received none, and expressed frustration that poorer areas bore the brunt of school closures.

publicComments.name: Pam Barish
publicComments.summary: 18-year kindergarten teacher asked the board to remember teachers' own health, family, and childcare challenges as they plan for reopening.

publicComments.name: Mohamed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Roy Cloud second-grade parent urged the district to evaluate technology platforms carefully, noting Google Meet was less effective than Zoom and Seesaw for his son's distance learning.

publicComments.name: Michelle Buetler
publicComments.summary: RSP teacher encouraged the district to inform parents not to purchase devices, urged equity in Spanish-language communication, and raised concerns about the workload and complexity of hybrid teaching.

publicComments.name: Michelle Ortez
publicComments.summary: Teacher and parent expressed concern about plans to reduce social distancing or increase class ratios, and urged the board to prioritize the safety of teachers and students over returning to campus.

publicComments.name: Michelle Torrido
publicComments.summary: Middle school teacher described her journey from technology novice to achieving 90% student participation in distance learning, and stated she would prefer to continue distance learning rather than police safety protocols in person.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Parent stated she plans to keep her child home until a vaccine is available and suggested the district allow parents to pre-register for the at-home distance learning option now to better plan classroom capacity.

publicComments.name: Devin Mullane
publicComments.summary: Parent raised concerns about teacher workload in a hybrid model, suggested alternative scheduling options, asked about cost savings from campus closure, and questioned the choice of Chromebooks versus iPads.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: First and sixth grade parent expressed gratitude for the tablet announcement for younger grades and raised concerns about dual immersion programs losing language exposure during distance learning.

publicComments.name: Robin Estrada
publicComments.summary: Roosevelt campus monitor described pre-COVID problems with locked or broken bathrooms limiting handwashing access for students, urging the district to ensure functional bathrooms as part of reopening safety planning.

publicComments.name: Shawna Hackworth
publicComments.summary: Parent requested the district add parental content monitoring (such as Bark for Schools) to Chromebooks and provide training for young students on using Google platforms.
